text: True or False: Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem states that a consistent theory T strong enough to formalize arithmetic can prove the sentence Con(T) expressing its own consistency.
explanation: False — the Second Theorem states the opposite: T ⊬ Con(T); no such consistent theory can prove its own consistency. This is what ended Hilbert's program of establishing consistency by means formalizable within the system (e.g. ZFC cannot prove Con(ZFC)).
